Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task

Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# task-de15989a — slide a shape toward a full-line divider, add color-8 trailing line

## Confirmed rule (three demos + accepted test, 2026-09-30)
An input is a uniform-background grid with a full-width or full-height straight divider of color 2, and a patterned object/region on one side. Translate the object toward the divider by the minimum number of cells needed for its bounding box to become immediately adjacent to the divider, without crossing/overlapping the divider. Then paint color 8 along the entire grid-spanning line at the object's final trailing edge, i.e. the edge opposite the divider (the line immediately behind the translated shape). Preserve the rest of the grid, including the divider and all details/holes within the object. Output dimensions unchanged. If the object is already adjacent to the divider, translate zero cells and paint the adjacent full line on the opposite side of the object.

The edge line is grid-spanning: vertical line for vertical translation/horizontal divider; horizontal line for horizontal translation/vertical divider. The object itself is translated exactly, preserving internal background-colored gaps as part of its pattern. Translation stops at first contact with divider, not an arbitrary fixed one-cell step.

## Demonstrations
1. Demo 1, 19x28, background 0. Full vertical color-2 divider at column 25. Pattern color 7 lies to its left, with bbox r2–15, c14–23; one empty column separates it from divider. Output pattern is shifted right one column (to c15–24), and full column c14 is color 8. Other cells unchanged.
2. Demo 2, 21x22, background 6. Full horizontal color-2 divider at row 8. Pattern 5 bbox r3–6, c14–18, with row 7 gap. Output shape shifted down one row to r4–7; full row 3 becomes color 8. Other cells unchanged.
3. Demo 3, 14x20, background 1. Full horizontal color-2 divider at row 6. Sparse zero-valued pattern occupies rows 10–13; shift it upward three rows until its top is at row 7 (one row below divider). Full row 11, immediately behind the translated pattern, becomes 8. Details of the pattern are preserved after shift; other cells unchanged.

## Accepted test confirmation
Test was 28x25, background 3, color-2 full horizontal divider at row 22. The large irregular color-5 pattern occupied rows 13–21 and was already immediately adjacent to divider, so it did not move. Correct output changed only row 12 to all 8s; all other rows, including pattern with its holes, divider row 22, and background, were unchanged. The task was accepted after two incorrect guesses. This definitively confirms zero translation when already touching, and line 8 belongs immediately on the far side/opposite-divider edge of the unchanged object.

## Solve checklist
- Find the full line of color 2 and determine which side contains the patterned object.
- Determine the object's bounding box (include patterned background-colored holes; infer its full shape from non-background cells) and slide toward divider until nearest bbox edge is one cell away.
- Translate the entire pattern cell-for-cell, not just the colored cells as separate points.
- Paint a full perpendicular color-8 line at the translated object's far edge, opposite the divider. Preserve everything else.
- Validate the exact translation distance: demo 1 and 2 moved one cell, demo 3 moved three, accepted test moved zero.
